To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified proteins that bind trivalent and glutathione- conjugated trivalent arsenics, which are more toxic than pentavalent arsenics.

the binding of proteins to trivalent and glutathione-bound trivalent arsenicals in human hepatocellular carcinoma cells is not solely dependent on the vicinal cysteine residues in the target proteins.

we identified proteins that bind to pentavalent and trivalent arsenicals, but the proteins that bind to glutathione conjugates of arsenicals were different from those that bind to trivalent or pentavalent arsenics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of proteins that bind to trivalent and glutathione-arsenicals.
the identification of arsenic-binding proteins in human hepatic cells.
the binding of trivalent and glutathione conjugated arsenicals to proteins in the cytosolic fraction of human hepatocarcinaoma cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
arsenicals bind a wide range of proteins, and that these proteins are not limited to proteins containing vicinal cysteine residues.
trivalent arsenical-binding proteins are cysteine-rich and that glutathione-conjucated trivalent arsenical binding proteins are not necessarily cysteine-rich.

arsenicals bind to a variety of proteins in hepatic cytosol and that the binding affinity and specificity depend on the chemical structure of the arsenical and on the amino acid sequence of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
arsenicals react with a number of proteins in hepatic cytosol.
the binding of arsenicals to proteins depends on the oxidation state of arsenic and the chemical nature of the protein, including the amino acid residues surrounding the cysteines.

the binding of arsenicals to cysteine-rich cellular proteins is a complex process and that the binding affinity and specificity are affected by the chemical forms of arsenicals as well as by the structures of the proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the binding of arsenicals to proteins is a complex process that is influenced by the chemical structure of the arsenicals, the chemical structure and location of cysteine residues in the proteins, and the amino acids that are adjacent to the vicinal cysteine residues.
the binding of arsenicals to proteins in hepatic cytosol is a complex process that involves not only the thiol groups but also other amino acids in the protein structure.
the toxicity of arsenic is not only due to the direct binding of arsenic to proteins but also to the binding of arsenic metabolites to proteins.
